news.title: Lowe's wants your kid to skip college for a six-figure job
news.summary: Lowe's wants your kid to skip college for a six-figure job
news.full_text:
While artificial intelligence (AI) might be able to write a bad version of this article at a much lower price than what a human writer charges, the technology has its limitations.

"AI, without question, is changing work," Lowe's CEO Marvin Ellison told The Wall Street Journal. "But somebody will still be required to crawl under your sink and fix a leak, get your HVAC working, or do construction on a data center."

"Low labor force participation and skills gaps are especially acute in manufacturing, construction, and other skilled trades, where for every five workers who retire, only two replacements enter the workforce. By 2030, an estimated 2.1 million skilled trades jobs could go unfilled, with potential economic losses reaching $1 trillion annually," according to the U.S. Department of Education.

The Lowe's Foundation has launched the Building Futures Skilled Trades Coalition, the largest cross-sector skilled trades coalition in U.S. history, to help train and develop one million people for skilled trades careers by 2035.

This national alliance is backed by over 75 American educators, businesses, workforce organizations, industry vendors, and stakeholders across the skilled trades ecosystem, including corporate leaders such as Nvidia, AT&T, Bank of America, Carrier, General Motors, DeWalt, and Duke Energy.

"The next industrial revolution won't be built by algorithms alone. It will be built by the millions of skilled trade professionals who power, connect, and move this country forward," Ellison said in a press release.

Change the perception of careers in the skilled trades by challenging outdated narratives that position college as the default path to success.

Invest, connect, and scale proven training and credentialing solutions by bringing together educators, businesses, workforce organizations, corporate leaders, industry vendors, and other stakeholders to address shared workforce challenges and expand what works.

news.title: Intel’s AI Tailwinds Are Real. Mizuho Cut the Target Anyway.
news.summary: Intel’s AI Tailwinds Are Real. Mizuho Cut the Target Anyway.
news.full_text:
On September 3, Mizuho lowered the price target on Intel Corporation (NASDAQ:INTC) to $92 from $109. Mizuho's note reads more bullish on INTC's business than the price target suggests, but the firm is stopping short of turning bullish.

The firm noted multiple operating tailwinds working in favor of Intel, namely Agentic AI demand, enterprise server refreshes, and improving PC demand and potential foundry growth. However, CPU supply constraints and near-term multiple compression on Agentic AI stocks keep the Wall Street firm on the sidelines.

The first operating tailwind Mizuho notes for Intel is server OEMs reporting accelerating Agentic-AI demand into 2027. This demand is not only driving higher token usage but also improving CPU to GPU ratio in AI infrastructure, i.e. the ratio of CPUs to GPUs deployed in servers. This is an important aspect considering CPUs act as managers and directors to GPUs even though GPUs do the heavy weight work.

Recent server refreshes are also driving some of the upside for Intel. Meanwhile, corporate PC refresh activity is also beginning to materialize. On the foundry side, the firm expects Advanced Packaging Revenue to reach $3.5 billion by 2029, with external foundry customers for Intel's 14A process likely to add another $3.5 billion.

While stronger demand is a good sign, CPU supply constraints could be a problem for Intel if the company is unable to fully meet improving demand. Mizuho noted that Intel's CPU customers may face supply constraints that could lead them to face shortages next year.

While supply shortages are usually an avenue for supporting prices, they may also limit unit growth and pave way for competitors.

A valuation problem also exists for Intel, as it does for other Agentic AI stocks. However, it is worth noting that while tailwinds are supported by specific figures or percentages, the reported justification for cutting the price target appears to reflect on multiple compression for Agentic AI stocks. This makes the call less about deteriorating fundamentals and more about how much investors should be paying for those fundamentals today.

Smart money positioning has become considerably more constructive on Intel. As per Insider Monkey's database tracking more than a thousand hedge funds, 138 hedge funds held INTC at the end of the second quarter, up from 112 in the prior one.
